scope: Independent observer meta-tests and a real narrow product-harness smoke; not a 57-ID acceptance campaign

interfaces.session: DockerBrowserSession(actual RuntimeSession, origin=runtime.origin).start(); endpoint private; close(); receipt without WS token
interfaces.driver: chromium.connect(endpoint, timeout=10000, expose_network=''); never host launch for supervised/live_sqlite products
interfaces.local_exception: trusted_fixture_local_browser=True explicitly supplied by a supervisor-owned fixture constructor only; ignored when live_sqlite requires absent runtime; no failure fallback
interfaces.lifecycle: Close contexts and browser connection, stop/remove exact owned browser, then close owned control tunnel; parent untouched
interfaces.product_scripts: No product config, scripts or imports on host; JS renderer inside separate hardened Docker container

tests.scope: 40 structural negatives + real Docker OS proof + real Argon2/UI/API/SQLite/persistence smoke + 11 tunnel tests
46 structural/cancellation/token tests + real Docker OS proof + 11 tunnel tests, after final argv/env checks

limits: Docker daemon, Linux kernel and the pinned trusted factory image remain trusted dependencies; not a general container-escape proof.
Chromium internal sandbox is not qualified. The outer NETNONE/nonroot/readonly/cap-drop/no-new-privileges boundary is independently inspected.
The browser shares the product's loopback namespace, not PID/IPC/filesystem namespaces. The exact product and private browser control remain reachable there.
No generated-product acceptance is inferred from the smoke or these fixture observations. External independent source/profile reviews and a same-snapshot full campaign remain required.
